text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

-Governor of the Arctic island of Spitzbergen Ann-Kristen Olsen says she has no regrets in the handling of the recovery operation following the crash of a Russian airliner, which slammed into a mountain side last Thursday killing all 141 people on board. Tempers in the Russian community of Barentsburg, where many of the dead lived, were calmer on Monday after angry scenes against Norwegian authorities at the weekend.

-Construction and offshore group Aker is considering a merge with Recource Group International (RGI), which ownes nearly 40 percent of Aker's shares. Together, Aker and RGI have a total turnover on 22 billion crowns a year.

-State-owned energy producer Statkraft is a winner among the power companies this year. Statkraft posted net profits of 630 million crowns in the first six months of 1996 against 93 million crowns in the same period last year.
-Norway's 16 largest newspapers have lost 250,000 readers during the last year.

-Shares in drilling and offshsore service company Transocean climbed six crowns yesterday to 176,50 crowns. The company is planning a merge with U.S. driller Sonat, which gained $2 3/8 in the U.S. on Friday to close at $54 5/8.
